content.title: About
content.content: Ground pork is minced pork meat obtained from various cuts of the carcass, most commonly from the shoulder, neck, and thigh. It has a soft texture, mild pork flavor, and a characteristic aroma. Ground pork is used in a wide range of dishes: patties, meatballs, sauces, fillings for pies and dumplings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground pork is often added to sausages and hot dogs to improve juiciness and flavor.
Many traditional dishes around the world feature ground pork, such as Polish kibbeh, Italian ragù, and Russian kotleti.
Ground pork can be sold lean or with added fat, which influences taste and cooking properties.
When stored properly, fresh ground pork lasts up to 2 days in the fridge and up to 3 months in the freezer.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Ground pork provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and B12, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation, and wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and a small amount of carbohydrate supplies sustained energy, useful for active individuals.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Ground pork can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella and E. coli. It must be cooked to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Fat‑rich ground pork may contribute to elevated cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork proteins.

items.title: Added sodium in seasoned mixes
items.content: Pre‑seasoned ground pork can contain high salt levels, which is a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ground pork can be sautéed, braised, baked, or boiled. It is used for patties, meatballs, sauces, pie fillings, dumplings, and stuffed vegetables. If a leaner option is desired, excess fat can be drained after cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh ground pork in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw completely in the fridge before use.
